notes: This dataset tracks older AMD Vega/Vega20 GPUs whose HBM/HBM2 capacity and bandwidth can make them interesting local-LLM experiments at secondary-market prices.

Current ROCm system-requirements documentation marks gfx900 and gfx906 generations unsupported. These records therefore do not treat historical ROCm capability as current framework support; exact older ROCm, Vulkan, OpenCL, or community-runtime compatibility must be tested.

Marketplace prices are point-in-time observations. Model-fit guidance is approximate and depends on quantization, context/KV cache, runtime overhead, and whether model weights remain fully accelerator-resident.

software: historical ROCm support; current ROCm unsupported
hardware.software_lifecycle: AMD's current ROCm system-requirements tables mark MI25 / gfx900 unsupported. Historical software stacks or non-ROCm backends may work, but current prebuilt ROCm libraries must not be assumed compatible.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: 16GB HBM2 is suitable for many 7B-14B quantized models and some larger aggressively quantized models when context/KV-cache overhead is controlled. Capacity, not compute, is the main limiting factor for larger dense models.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF quantized models may be usable through compatible Vulkan/community backends
FP16 hardware throughput is strong for its age
Do not assume modern ROCm low-precision kernels or current PyTorch ROCm wheels support gfx900
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Experimental but unusually cheap. The attraction is 16GB HBM2 at roughly CA$100-class used pricing; current software support, passive cooling, and 300W peak power are major disadvantages.
physical_constraints: Passive server cooler needs high directed airflow
Large BAR / firmware compatibility can be problematic on some consumer systems
hardware.off_grid_notes: The very low purchase price is offset by a 300W peak board envelope and required forced airflow, making sustained solar/battery operation unattractive.

pricing.note: eBay.ca product page showed multiple MI25 16GB listings around CA$108.63, with higher tested listings also present. Shipping, seller location, condition, duties, and stock vary.

software: AMD Software: PRO Edition 26.Q1 on supported Windows platforms
historical/community compute backends; current ROCm not supported
hardware.software_lifecycle: AMD still publishes 2026 PRO Edition Windows drivers for WX 9100, but current ROCm support does not include gfx900. Graphics/OpenCL/Vulkan driver availability must not be confused with current ROCm/PyTorch support.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: 16GB HBM2 fits many 7B-14B quantized models. It is easier to integrate than MI25 because cooling is onboard, but current AI framework support is much weaker than modern RDNA/CDNA hardware.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF quantized models may be practical through compatible Vulkan/community backends
OpenCL remains available through current professional Windows drivers
Current ROCm/PyTorch support for gfx900 should not be assumed
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Interesting only at very low used prices. It combines active cooling, ECC HBM2, and 484GB/s bandwidth, but legacy software support limits it to experimental or carefully pinned environments.
physical_constraints: Six Mini DisplayPort outputs can be useful in workstation repurposing
hardware.off_grid_notes: 230W board power is better than MI25/Radeon VII but still high for continuous battery operation; active cooling makes integration easier than passive datacenter cards.

pricing.note: A pre-owned WX 9100 listing was observed at CA$170 in an active auction/search result. Auction pricing is not equivalent to a stable buy-it-now market value.

hardware.software_lifecycle: Radeon VII / gfx906 was deprecated in older ROCm releases and is absent/unsupported in current ROCm system requirements. Current graphics-driver availability does not imply current ROCm library support.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: 16GB limits model capacity to many 7B-14B-class quantized models, but 1TB/s-class HBM2 bandwidth is exceptionally high for the current used price and can make memory-bound kernels attractive when a working backend is available.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF k-quants may run through compatible Vulkan/community backends

Modern ROCm/PyTorch wheels should not be assumed compatible with gfx906

physical_constraints: Reference cards require substantial case airflow
Two auxiliary 8-pin connectors on reference design
Used cards may have mining/workstation history
hardware.off_grid_notes: Bandwidth-per-watt is respectable for a legacy card, but 300W board draw is too high for an efficient always-on off-grid node.

pricing.note: Toronto-area Radeon VII 16GB listings were observed around CA$350. Local-classified availability and condition can change quickly.

interconnect: Infinity Fabric Link; up to 168 GB/s peer-to-peer according to AMD launch materials
software: AMD Software: PRO Edition 26.Q1 on supported Windows platforms
historical ROCm support; current ROCm unsupported
hardware.software_lifecycle: AMD still distributes current professional Windows drivers for Radeon Pro VII, but current ROCm matrices mark gfx906 unsupported. Historical ROCm capability should not be presented as current PyTorch/ROCm support.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: 16GB constrains model size similarly to Radeon VII, while ~1TB/s HBM2 bandwidth and ECC are attractive for memory-bound inference experiments. Multi-GPU Infinity Fabric Link is application/runtime dependent and should not be treated as automatically pooled LLM VRAM.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF quantized models may be usable through compatible Vulkan/community backends
High HBM2 bandwidth is attractive for quantized decode when the backend supports the card
Do not assume current ROCm/PyTorch support for gfx906
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Niche/experimental. Technically excellent memory bandwidth per watt for its generation and easier workstation integration than passive Instinct cards, but software age and 16GB capacity sharply limit general recommendation value.
physical_constraints: Used professional cards may have long duty-cycle history
hardware.off_grid_notes: At 4GB/s of HBM bandwidth per board watt it is efficient by legacy standards, but a 250W board envelope is still substantial for battery-backed use.

pricing.note: A pre-owned Radeon Pro VII 16GB listing was observed around CA$626.18 plus shipping; new/other examples were higher. Marketplace prices vary widely.
